content: The University of Prince Edward Island (UPEI) is located in Charlottetown, Prince Edward Island, Canada. It was established in 1969 through the merger of two predecessor institutions, Prince of Wales College (PWC) and St. Dunstan's University (SDU). The current UPEI campus is situated on the former SDU campus. Graduates of SDU and PWC are among the faculty at UPEI, and the university is attended by children of current and former faculty and staff. Many families proudly maintain multi-generational alumni connections to the institution. The original SDU buildings in the central quad have been renovated to preserve their exterior aesthetic design while meeting modern standards. The C.A.W. MacLauchlan Arena and Aquatics Centre were completed in 2004. In 2006, a new residence facility, referred to as New Residence, was completed. In October 2004, UPEI announced plans to improve the aesthetics of modern buildings constructed since the merger, ensuring they align with the original SDU design. This plan also considered the construction of a new residence building, expansions to the Atlantic Veterinary College, and the development of a new National Research Council of Canada facility. The current President of UPEI is H. Wade MacLauchlan, who has held the position since October 3, 1999. The current Chancellor is William E. (Bill) Andrew. Over the past three decades, UPEI has significantly expanded its academic offerings. Bachelor's degree programs, many with honors options, are available in Arts, Science, Business Administration, Education, and Nursing. Co-op programs have been introduced in Business Administration, Computer Science, Physics, and Dietetics. The university has added a Faculty of Veterinary Medicine and two schools, Business Administration and Nursing. Graduate programs, including Master's and Doctoral degrees, were first introduced through the Atlantic Veterinary College. In 1999, a Master of Science degree was offered through the Faculty of Science, and the first students were admitted to the new Master of Education program. UPEI also offers a Master of Arts in Island Studies. Since 1998, the Centre for Conflict Resolution Studies has provided courses leading to a Certificate in Conflict Resolution Studies. The faculty association and administration have experienced contract disputes. The Faculty Association had been without a contract since June 2005 and voted overwhelmingly in favor of a strike, which lasted from March 21 to April 5, 2006. UPEI has recently gained recognition in the media. While it was previously ranked low on Maclean's Magazine's list of top Canadian schools, it has made significant progress in recent years. UPEI is currently ranked 5 among top undergraduate schools in Canada, surpassing most universities in the Maritime region and closely competing with St. Francis Xavier University in Antigonish, Nova Scotia. The UPEI Student Union Inc. publishes a newspaper called The Cadre. The paper gained attention for being the first North American publication to print the controversial Muhammad cartoons from Jyllands-Posten. The university administration ordered the removal of the paper from campus circulation, citing concerns that publishing the caricatures represented a reckless invitation to public disorder and humiliation. The university acknowledged the debates surrounding press freedom and responsibility generated by this issue. In January 2007, CBC News reported that the editorial staff of The Cadre sought to end its relationship with the Student Union. In March 2007, CBC News reported that the Student Union was considering transferring responsibility for the paper to the UPEI Independent Student Media Society (ISMS). The ISMS planned to reduce the number of staff at The Cadre from twelve to six and decrease its publication frequency from twice a month to once a month. The UPEI Panthers have ten athletic teams competing in the Atlantic University Sport (AUS) and Canadian Interuniversity Sport (CIS) leagues. These teams include men's and women's ice hockey, soccer, basketball, and rugby, as well as women's volleyball and field hockey.
